The 5.9/10 restrictiveness score reflects the balanced approach: while the target must obtain parent consent for specified actions, the consent standard is reasonable, ordinary course operations continue, and the target retains operational control. This framework is market-standard for public company M&A transactions.

The clauses protect buyers from adverse tax settlements or strategic tax decisions that could increase post-closing tax liabilities or eliminate valuable tax assets. The 7.6/10 restrictiveness reflects the balance between absolute prohibitions on material tax decisions and practical exceptions for routine matters and pre-disclosed reserves.

The 6.5/10 restrictiveness reflects this balanced approach typical of negotiated M&A agreements.

The high restrictiveness score reflects that these clauses eliminate any potential loopholes in the covenant structure.
